nodes.summary: For a subset $X$ of a group $G$, let $C_G(X)$ be its centralizer, the subgroup of elements of $G$ that commute with every element of $X$. The group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on centralizers if every nonempty set of such centralizers has a minimal element with respect to inclusion; equivalently, there is no infinite strictly descending chain $C_G(X_0) > C_G(X_1) > \cdots$ of centralizers.
nodes.title: Minimal condition on centralizers (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: The Hirsch–Plotkin radical of a group $G$ is the subgroup generated by all locally nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$. By the Hirsch–Plotkin theorem it is the largest locally nilpotent normal subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Hirsch–Plotkin radical

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is hypercentral if for every proper normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ there is some $g \in G$ with $g \notin N$ and $g h g^{-1} h^{-1} \in N$ for all $h \in G$; that is, every nontrivial quotient $G/N$ has nontrivial centre (equivalently, the transfinite upper central series of $G$ reaches $G$).
nodes.title: Hypercentral group (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is locally nilpotent if for every finite subset $S \subseteq G$ the subgroup generated by $S$ is nilpotent, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent group (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is locally nilpotent when every subgroup generated by finitely many elements of $N$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent subgroup

nodes.summary: Every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.16 (F. O. Wagner) in the affirmative (V. V. Bludov, 1998).
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent groups with the minimal condition on centralizers are hypercentral

nodes.summary: The proposition that every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.16 (Wagner)
